case_scope: United States collective bargaining and wealth formation

workplace_power_gate.note: BLS 2025 union evidence keeps workplace power below a national comfort pass; NLRB performance evidence is needed to determine whether formal organizing rights become contracts/remedies.

collective_bargaining_coverage.note: Bargaining coverage remains too narrow to carry a broad predistribution/wealth-formation verdict, especially outside the public sector. Rev0344 unused-source burn-down: OECD firm-level wage-inequality evidence is now bound to the workplace-power proof burden. Rev0344 unused-source burn-down: OECD collective-bargaining/social-dialogue evidence is now bound to the collective-coverage burden.

union_density_and_access.note: Union density must be scored by sector, earnings distribution, region, race, gender, and first-contract conversion rather than treated as a generic wage premium. Rev0344 unused-source burn-down: OECD bargaining-coverage data is now bound to union-density and access rather than left unused.

wage_floor_adequacy.note: Minimum-wage and wage-floor adequacy requires cost-of-living and household-composition adjustment.

wage_theft_and_pay_remedy_access.note: The case cannot pass until NLRB/WHD/private-right enforcement evidence shows workers can convert rights into timely backpay, reinstatement, bargaining orders, or settlements.

worker_voice_in_firm_governance.note: Worker voice is not proven by union density alone; certification requires evidence that voice changes scheduling, discipline, pay, safety, technology, and grievance outcomes.

proof_debt: private-sector bargaining coverage by wage tier and sector
unfair-labor-practice remedy conversion and backpay collection
union/nonunion wage and benefit effects after local cost adjustment
worker voice over scheduling, discipline, surveillance, and technology deployment

gate_14_workplace_power.why: Coverage and remedy-conversion evidence is still too thin to certify workplace power as a national wealth-formation rail.

gate_11_enforcement.why: Union rights need timely election, first-contract, reinstatement, bargaining-order, and backpay conversion proof.

evidence_debt_register.question: private-sector bargaining coverage by wage tier and sector
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Use BLS union-membership tables plus NLRB election/certification data to estimate which workers actually reach bargaining coverage.

evidence_debt_register.question: first-contract success, delay, and abandonment
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Collect NLRB first-contract timelines and abandonment rates before counting union access as usable workplace power.

evidence_debt_register.question: unfair-labor-practice remedy conversion and backpay collection
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Measure whether remedies are timely and collectable enough to prevent employer delay from washing out worker claims.

evidence_debt_register.question: local cost/saveable-room calibration
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Estimate whether wage/benefit premiums survive rent, transportation, childcare, healthcare, and debt-service burdens.

evidence_debt_register.question: worker voice over scheduling, discipline, and technology
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Collect contract clauses and enforcement outcomes for scheduling, discipline, algorithmic management, and safety.

policy_pathway: Treat organizing access, first-contract timelines, and enforceable backpay/reinstatement as wealth-threshold evidence rather than labor-law background.
Private-sector bargaining coverage, first-contract conversion, and remedy collection must improve before Gate 14 can move from blocked to watch.
